subject: Error in getOctD(x, offset, len) : invalid octal digit

messages.author: d7a934c791b29498
messages.subject: Error in getOctD(x, offset, len) : invalid octal digit
parts:
I have tried using sudo R CMD INSTALL to install two versions of rmr2, namely 2.2.2 and 2.3.0

Due to firewall issues, I downloaded first to Windows.  Windows was able to recognize the tar.gz as a zip, but 7z was not able to unzip it on Windows.

I used FileZilla to transfer these to a Linux 64-bit machine running CentOS behind a firewall.  However, when I tried sudo R CMD INSTALL, I got:


Error in getOctD(x, offset, len) : invalid octal digit

here is the first error:
-bash-4.1$ sudo R CMD INSTALL ./rmr2_2.3.0.tar.gz

Error in getOctD(x, offset, len) : invalid octal digit

gunzip was able to unzip to a tar, but tar could not process the result:

-bash-4.1$ tar xvf rmr2_2.3.0.tar
tar: This does not look like a tar archive

My only guess is that because I am using a Windows machine to grab the tar.gz, Windows is somehow corrupting the file.

Any input is welcome.
Thanks.

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1017] Error in getOctD(x, offset, len) : invalid octal digit
parts:
I am not sure what's going on here, but there is one bit in your message that is wrong, that is confusing the zip format and the gzip format. Despite the name similarity they are distinct formats. So "windows was able to recognize the tar.gz as a zip" is already wrong. Maybe the command 'file' in Unix will help you tell what's in that file, but sure you need to download it again in some other way.


Antonio
